claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is in a single-phase hexagonal state.
Rapid deposition leaves the alloy with substantial local chemical disorder.
Rapid deposition leaves the alloy with substantial microstructural strain.
Mild post-deposition annealing just below the ordering transition increases atomic ordering.
Mild post-deposition annealing relieves internal stresses.
A suitable mild anneal can increase ordering and relieve stress without causing grain coarsening.
Local chemical ordering is associated with the distribution of lattice strains and defects in the hexagonal phase.
Partial atomic reordering and reduced local strain smooth the magnetostructural coupling.
Smoother magnetostructural coupling reduces the abruptness of the first-order transition.
Reducing the transition abruptness decreases hysteresis during low-field cycling.
Partial reordering and strain relief can reduce hysteresis while retaining a significant magnetocaloric effect.
The as-deposited baseline has a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with a large but highly hysteretic magnetic entropy change.
Annealed samples will have a broader magnetocaloric transition profile than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will have a lower peak magnetic entropy change per field step than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit a smaller hysteresis-loop area during cyclic magnetization measurements.
The predicted behavior should hold near the intrinsic transition temperature at applied fields around or below 1 T.
The predictions apply to similarly rapid-deposited thin films or rapidly quenched deposits rather than bulk ingots, and may fail after excessive annealing or for substantially different compositions.
